quests.instruction: Clap the beats in “table”. How many syllables does it have?
quests.hint: Each beat has one vowel sound. Clap as you say ta-ble.
quests.explanation: “Table” has 2 syllables: ta-ble. Each syllable is a beat in the word.
quests.funFact: Each syllable is one beat of a word. Clapping the beats helps you read long words one chunk at a time.

quests.instruction: Which word has just one syllable and a silent e?
quests.hint: Clap each word, then look for an e at the end that you cannot hear.
quests.explanation: “Plane” has one beat and a silent e that makes the a long. “Planet” has two syllables, and “plant” has one but no silent e.

quests.instruction: Which word has three syllables?
quests.hint: Clap each word and count the beats.
quests.explanation: “Banana” has 3 syllables: ba-na-na. “Basket” has 2 and “bread” has 1.

quests.instruction: How many syllables are in “butterfly”?
quests.hint: Break the word into chunks as you say it.
quests.explanation: “Butterfly” has 3 syllables: but-ter-fly.
quests.funFact: A word can have one beat, like cat, or many beats, like butterfly.

quests.instruction: Which word has the most syllables?
quests.hint: Clap each word and compare.
quests.explanation: “Elephant” has 3 syllables. “Pencil” has 2 and “ant” has 1.

quests.instruction: Every syllable has one vowel sound. How many vowel sounds are in “rabbit”?
quests.hint: Say rab-bit and count the vowel sounds.
quests.explanation: “Rabbit” has 2 syllables, so it has 2 vowel sounds: /a/ and /i/.

quests.instruction: Which shows “sunset” split into syllables?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly. Where does the first beat end?
quests.explanation: “Sunset” is made of two words, sun and set, so it divides sun-set.

quests.instruction: Which shows “napkin” split into syllables?
quests.hint: Look for the two consonants in the middle and split between them.
quests.explanation: “Napkin” has two consonants in the middle, p and k. We divide between them: nap-kin.
quests.funFact: When a word has two consonants in the middle, you can usually divide between them.

quests.instruction: Which shows “happen” divided into syllables?
quests.hint: The two p letters are in the middle. Where do you split?
quests.explanation: “Happen” divides between the two p letters: hap-pen.

quests.instruction: Put the syllables together: “win” + “dow”. Which word do you make?
quests.hint: Say each chunk, then glue them together.
quests.explanation: “Win” + “dow” makes “window”. “Winter” has a different second chunk.
quests.funFact: In “window”, the first beat is a little stronger: WIN-dow.

quests.instruction: Say “picnic” slowly. What is the first syllable?
quests.hint: Listen for where the first beat ends.
quests.explanation: “Picnic” divides as pic-nic. The first syllable is pic.

quests.instruction: Which word has the syllables “sis” and “ter”?
quests.hint: Blend the two chunks together.
quests.explanation: “Sis” + “ter” makes “sister”. The second syllable has an r-controlled vowel.

quests.instruction: Each syllable has one vowel sound. Which vowel sound do you hear in the first syllable of “napkin”?
quests.hint: Say nap, then the rest of the word.
quests.explanation: In “nap-kin”, the first syllable is nap, with short a.
quests.funFact: Napkin, pumpkin and robin each have two vowel sounds, so each has two syllables.

quests.instruction: What vowel sound do you hear in the second syllable of “robin”?
quests.hint: Say rob-in. Listen to the last chunk.
quests.explanation: In “rob-in”, the second syllable has short i.

quests.instruction: How many vowel sounds does “pumpkin” have?
quests.hint: Say pump-kin and count each vowel sound.
quests.explanation: “Pumpkin” has 2 syllables, so it has 2 vowel sounds: /u/ and /i/.

quests.instruction: A closed syllable ends with a consonant and has a short vowel, like “nap”. Which word is made of two closed syllables?
quests.hint: Check both syllables. Does each one end with a consonant?
quests.explanation: In “nap-kin”, both syllables end with a consonant and have short vowels. “Table” and “robot” have open or special syllables.
quests.funFact: Rabbit, napkin, sunset and basket each have two closed syllables.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a closed syllable?
quests.hint: Look for a syllable that ends with a consonant.
quests.explanation: “Dig” ends with g, a consonant, so it is closed. “Go” and “me” end with a vowel.

quests.instruction: The first syllable of “rabbit” is closed. What sound does its vowel make?
quests.hint: Say rab. Is the vowel short or long?
quests.explanation: In the closed syllable rab, the vowel is short: /a/.

quests.instruction: An open syllable ends with a vowel, and the vowel says its name, like “go”. Which word starts with an open syllable?
quests.hint: Say each word. Which first syllable ends with a vowel sound?
quests.explanation: “Robot” divides as ro-bot. The first syllable is open, so o says its name.
quests.funFact: Robot, tiger, music and paper all begin with an open syllable and a long vowel.

quests.instruction: In “tiger”, the first syllable is open. Which vowel sound does it have?
quests.hint: Say ti-ger. Does the first vowel say its name?
quests.explanation: In “ti-ger”, the first syllable is open, so i says long i.

quests.instruction: Which word starts with an open syllable?
quests.hint: Divide each word. Which first syllable ends with a vowel?
quests.explanation: “Baby” divides as ba-by, so the first syllable is open. “Bunny” and “basket” start with closed syllables.

quests.instruction: Which word has a closed first syllable?
quests.hint: Say each word. Does the vowel in the first syllable say its name?
quests.explanation: “Robin” divides as rob-in with a short o. “Robot” divides as ro-bot with long o.

quests.instruction: Which word has an open first syllable?
quests.hint: Split each word and check whether the first chunk ends with a vowel sound.
quests.explanation: “Music” divides as mu-sic, with long u. “Muffin” and “mitten” start with closed syllables.

quests.instruction: The word “paper” divides as pa-per. Which vowel sound does the first syllable have?
quests.hint: Is the first syllable open or closed?
quests.explanation: “Pa” is an open syllable, so the a says its name.
quests.funFact: Open syllables often have long vowels and closed syllables often have short vowels.

quests.instruction: Which word is read “hap” + “py”?
quests.hint: Say the two chunks and blend them.
quests.explanation: “Hap” + “py” makes “happy”. The final y says long e.
quests.funFact: Words like happy, rabbit and pillow have two matching consonants in the middle, so you split between them.

quests.instruction: Which word is made from “pump” + “kin”?
quests.hint: Blend the chunks together.
quests.explanation: “Pump” + “kin” makes “pumpkin”, a two-syllable word.

quests.instruction: Which word is made from “car” + “pet”?
quests.hint: Say each chunk, then glue them.
quests.explanation: “Car” + “pet” makes “carpet”. The first syllable has the /ar/ sound.

quests.instruction: Clap “dinosaur”. How many beats do you count?
quests.hint: Clap the beats as you say it.
quests.explanation: “Dinosaur” has 3 syllables: di-no-saur.
quests.funFact: The word dinosaur comes from Greek words meaning “terrible lizard”.

quests.instruction: Which word is divided correctly?
quests.hint: Divide between the two consonants in the middle.
quests.explanation: “Helmet” divides between l and m: hel-met.

quests.instruction: Which word has two closed syllables?
quests.hint: Check both syllables. Do they end with consonants?
quests.explanation: “Sun-set” has two closed syllables. “Tiger” and “music” start with open syllables.
